p.seg: The Way that can be spoken of
is not the eternal Way.
The name that can be named
is not the eternal name.
Nameless, it is the beginning of heaven and earth;
Named, it is the mother of all things.
Therefore, constantly without desire, observe its subtlety;
Constantly with desire, observe its manifestations.
These two arise together but have different names.
Together they are called mysterious.
Mysterious and even more mysterious,
the gateway to all subtleties.
When all under heaven know beauty as beauty,
there is already ugliness.
When all know good as good,
there is already not-good.
Thus being and non-being give birth to each other,
difficult and easy complete each other,
long and short contrast with each other,
high and low lean on each other,
sound and voice harmonize with each other,
front and back follow each other.
Therefore the sage dwells in the action of non-action,
and practices the teaching of no words.
The myriad things arise, and he does not refuse them.
He gives them life but does not take possession of them.
He acts but does not rely on his own ability.
When his work is accomplished, he does not claim credit for it.
It is precisely because he does not claim credit
That his achievements remain with him.
Not exalting the worthy,
keeps the people from contention;
Not prizing rare treasures,
keeps the people from stealing.
Not displaying what is desirable,
keeps the people's hearts from confusion.
Therefore the sage's governance:
Empties their minds,
Fills their bellies;
Weakens their ambitions,
Strengthens their bones.
Constantly keeps the people without knowledge and without desire.
Makes it so that those with knowledge dare not act.
Acts through non-action,
Then nothing remains ungoverned.
The Dao is empty, yet when used, it may not be exhausted.
Deep, it seems like the ancestor of all things.
It blunts its sharpness,
untangles its knots;
it harmonizes its light,
and blends with its dust.
So profound, it seems to exist or not.
I do not know whose child it is;
it appears before the Divine Emperor.
Heaven and Earth are not benevolent,
treating all things as straw dogs.
The sage is not benevolent,
treating the people as straw dogs.
Between Heaven and Earth,
is it not like a bellows?
Empty yet never exhausted,
moving and producing more.
Too much talk often leads to exhaustion,
better to hold fast to the center.
The valley spirit never dies;
It is called the mysterious female.
The gate of the mysterious female
Is called the root of heaven and earth.
Dimly visible, it seems as if it were there,
Yet use will never drain it.
Heaven and earth are enduring and everlasting.
The reason why heaven and earth can be enduring and everlasting
is that they do not give birth to themselves;
hence, they can live long.
Thus, the sage
puts himself last yet finds himself first,
disregards his own life yet his life is preserved.
Is it not because of his selflessness?
Therefore, he can accomplish his private ends.
The highest good is like water.
Water is good at benefiting all things
without contending,
and stays in places that people disdain.
Therefore it is close to the Way.
In dwelling, be good at choosing the right place;
in heart, be good at staying deep;
in giving, be good at showing benevolence;
in speech, be good at keeping promises;
in governing, be good at achieving order;
in affairs, be good at exercising ability;
in action, be good at seizing the right timing.
It is precisely because one does not contend
that one is without blame.
To hold until full,
It is better to stop in time.
To hammer until sharp,
Cannot be long maintained.
With a hall full of gold and jade,
None can keep them secure.
Wealth and honor accompanied by arrogance,
Bring upon themselves misfortune.
When the work is done, retire;
This is the Way of Heaven.
Can you keep the soul and the body as one without separation?
Can you concentrate your breath to achieve softness like a baby?
Can you cleanse your inner vision until it is free of flaws?
In loving the people and governing the state, can you do so without cunning knowledge?
When the gates of heaven open and close, can you remain in the feminine?
With understanding that reaches in all directions, can you be without knowledge?
To produce and to rear,
to produce, but not to take possession,
to act, but not to rely on one's ability,
to lead, but not to master,
this is called profound and secret virtue.
Thirty spokes
share one hub;
it is in its emptiness
that the utility of the carriage lies.
Clay is kneaded to make a vessel;
it is in its emptiness
that the utility of the vessel lies.
Doors and windows are cut to make a room;
it is in its emptiness
that the utility of the room lies.
Therefore, what exists serves for possession,
and what does not exist serves for utility.
The five colors blind the eyes.
The five tones deafen the ears.
The five flavors dull the palate.
Racing and hunting
madden the mind.
Rare treasures
impede one's actions.
Therefore the sage
governs by filling the belly,
not by captivating the eyes.
Thus he rejects that and takes this.
Favor and disgrace are both alarming,
just as one values great calamity as one's own body.
What is meant by "favor and disgrace are both alarming"?
Favor, when bestowed upon those below, is received with alarm and
lost with alarm.
This is called "favor and disgrace are both alarming."
What is meant by "valuing great calamity as one's own body"?
The reason I have great calamities
is because I have a body.
When I no longer have a body,
what calamities do I have?
Therefore, those who value their bodies as much as the world
can be entrusted with the world.
Those who love their bodies as much as the world
can be relied upon with the world.
Look at it but do not see it,
Name it "Elusive";
Listen to it but do not hear it,
Name it "Faint";
Grasp at it but do not hold it,
Name it "Subtle."
These three cannot be fully questioned,
So they merge into one.
First,
its upper part is not bright;
its lower part is not dark.
Endlessly it defies naming,
and returns to the state of nothingness.
This is called the form of the formless,
the image of the imageless.
This is called the elusive and vague.
Meeting it, one cannot see its front;
following it, one cannot see its back.
Hold fast to the Way of old,
to master the things of the present.
One can know the primeval beginning,
this is called the thread of the Way.
The ancient masters of the Way were subtle and profound,
mysteriously comprehending,
too deep to be understood.
Because they were beyond understanding,
I can only describe them with effort:
Cautious, like crossing a winter stream;
hesitant, like fearing their neighbors;
reserved, like a guest;
yielding, like ice about to melt.
Simple, like uncarved wood;
open, like a valley;
blended, like muddy water.
Who can, through stillness, gradually clarify the turbid?
Who can, through movement, gradually enliven the tranquil?
Those who uphold this Way
do not desire fullness.
Precisely because they do not desire fullness,
they can be worn yet renewed.
Attain the utmost emptiness,
Hold fast to stillness.
All things arise together,
And I watch their return.
Countless things flourish,
Each returns to its root.
Returning to the root is called stillness,
Stillness, this is called returning to destiny.
Returning to destiny is called the constant,
Knowing the constant is called clarity.
Not knowing the constant,
one acts recklessly and encounters misfortune.
Knowing the constant, one becomes all-embracing,
all-embracing leads to impartiality,
impartiality leads to sovereignty,
sovereignty leads to alignment with Heaven,
alignment with Heaven leads to the Way,
the Way leads to enduring longevity.
Thus, one remains free from harm throughout life.
The highest form of governance is when the people merely know of its existence;
The next is when they love and praise it;
The next is when they fear it,
And the next is when they despise it.
When trust is insufficient,
How can there be no distrust?
Be sparing and value your words.
When achievements are made and tasks accomplished,
The people all say, "We did it naturally."
When the great Way is abandoned,
there arises humanity and righteousness.
When wisdom and cunning appear,
there arises great hypocrisy.
When the six relations are at variance,
there arises filial piety and parental affection.
When the state and family are in chaos and disorder,
there arise loyal ministers.
Eliminate sagacity and discard wisdom,
and the people will benefit a hundredfold;
eliminate benevolence and discard righteousness,
and the people will return to filial piety and compassion;
eliminate skill and discard profit,
and there will be no thieves or robbers.
These three,
considered as embellishments are insufficient;
therefore, let the people have something to adhere to:
manifest simplicity and embrace genuineness,
reduce selfishness and diminish desires.
Abandon learning and have no worries.
How much difference is there
between "yes" and "yeah"?
How much difference is there
between good and evil?
What others fear,
one must also fear.
Vast and boundless, it has no end!
Vast and boundless, it seems never-ending!
The multitude are joyous and bustling,
as if feasting at a grand sacrifice,
as if ascending a tower in spring.
I alone am tranquil, showing no sign,
like an infant who has not yet learned to smile.
Listless, as if I had nowhere to return.
The multitude all have more than enough,
yet I alone seem to be left out.
My mind is that of a fool—
so muddled and confused!
The common people are bright and clear,
I alone seem dim and dull;
The common people are sharp and discerning,
I alone am muddled and confused.
Calm, like the deep sea;
Drifting, as if with no place to rest.
Everyone has a purpose,
But I alone am stubborn and seem uncouth.
I wish to be different from others,
And value nurturing from the source.
The appearance of great virtue
follows solely the Way.
The Way as a thing
is but vague and indistinct.
Indistinct and vague,
yet within it there are forms.
Vague and indistinct,
yet within it there are things.
Deep and obscure,
yet within it there is essence.
This essence is very real,
and within it there is truth.
From ancient times until now,
its name has never faded,
thereby revealing the origin of all things.
How do I know the state of all beginnings?
Through this.
To yield is to be whole;
To bend is to be straight;
To be hollow is to be filled;
To be worn is to be renewed.
To have little is to gain;
To have much is to be confused.
Therefore, the sage embraces the One
And becomes the model for the world.
Not seeing oneself, thus one is clear-sighted.
Not asserting oneself, thus one is distinguished.
Not praising oneself, thus one has merit.
Not boasting, thus one endures.
It is precisely because one does not contend
that no one in the world can contend with them.
What the ancients called
"yielding leads to wholeness,"
how could it be empty words?
Truly, wholeness returns to it.
Sparse words are natural.
Thus a gale does not last all morning,
A downpour does not last all day.
Who makes these?
Heaven and Earth.
If even Heaven and Earth cannot make them last long,
How much less can human beings?
Therefore, those who engage with the Dao,
are in harmony with the Dao;
those who engage with virtue, are in harmony with virtue;
those who engage with loss, are in harmony with loss.
Those in harmony with the Dao, the Dao also delights in gaining them;
those in harmony with virtue, virtue also delights in gaining them;
those in harmony with loss, loss also delights in gaining them.
When trust is insufficient, then there is distrust.
Those who stand on tiptoe do not stand firm;
those who stride cannot walk steadily.
Those who show off themselves are not enlightened;
those who assert themselves are not distinguished;
those who boast of themselves achieve no merit;
those who are self-conceited do not endure.
From the perspective of the Dào,
these are called "excess food and superfluous actions."
All things detest them,
thus those who possess the Dào do not dwell in such behaviors.
There is something formlessly created,
Born before Heaven and Earth.
Silent and void,
It stands alone and does not change,
Goes around and does not weary.
It is capable of being the mother of the world.
I do not know its name,
But style it 'the Way',
And I give it the makeshift name of 'the great'.
Being great, it is described as receding,
Receding, it is described as far away,
Being far away, it is described as turning back.
Thus the Dào is great,
Heaven is great,
Earth is great,
and the King is also great.
In the realm there are four great things,
and the King occupies one among them.
Humans model themselves on Earth,
Earth models itself on Heaven,
Heaven models itself on the Dào,
and the Dào models itself on nature.
Heaviness is the root of lightness,
Stillness is the master of restlessness.
Therefore, the sage travels all day
Without leaving the supply carts.
Though there may be splendid views,
He remains calm and detached.
How can the lord of ten thousand chariots
Treat the world lightly with his own person?
Lightness loses the root,
Restlessness loses the master.
A skilled traveler leaves no wheel ruts,
A skilled speaker makes no slips,
A skilled counter uses no tallies,
A skilled closer needs no bolt yet what is shut cannot be opened,
A skilled binder uses no cords yet what is tied cannot be undone.
Thus the sage is always good at saving people,
So there are no discarded people;
Always good at saving things,
So there are no discarded things;
This is called following enlightenment.
Thus, the good person is the teacher of the bad person;
the bad person is the resource for the good person.
If one does not value their teacher,
nor cherish their resource;
although wise, they are greatly deluded.
This is called the essential mystery.
Know the masculine,
Hold to the feminine,
And be the riverbed of the world.
Being the riverbed of the world,
The eternal virtue does not depart. The eternal virtue does not depart,
And return to the state of infancy.
Know the white,
Hold to the black,
And be the model of the world.
Being the model of the world,
The eternal virtue does not err. The eternal virtue does not err,
And return to the infinite.
Knowing honor,
yet keeping to disgrace,
one becomes the valley of the world.
Constant virtue is thus sufficient,
constant virtue is thus sufficient,
returning to the simplicity of the unhewn log.
When the simplicity is broken up, it becomes vessels.
The sage uses them,
and becomes the chief of officials.
Therefore, the great system
does not cut apart.
One who wishes to take the world and control it,
I see that he will not succeed.
The world is a sacred vessel,
and cannot be controlled.
Those who control it will ruin it;
those who grasp it will lose it.
Thus, some things lead while others follow,
some breathe gently while others blow fiercely,
some are strong while others are weak,
some are built up while others crumble.
Therefore, the sage discards excess,
discards extravagance,
discards extremes.
One who assists a ruler with the Dao
does not dominate the world by force of arms.
Such matters tend to rebound.
Where troops are stationed,
thorns and brambles grow.
In the wake of a great army
come years of famine.
Adeptness lies in achieving results and stopping,
not in daring to use it to seize dominance.
Achieve results but do not boast,
achieve results but do not flaunt,
achieve results but do not be arrogant.
Achieve results only when it is unavoidable:
this is called achieving results without force.
When things reach their prime, they begin to age.
This is called not following the Way.
Not following the Way leads to an early end.
For arms are instruments of ill omen,
and all things detest them.
Therefore, one who follows the Way does not rely on them.
The noble man, in his dwelling, values the left;
in employing arms, he values the right.
Hence, arms are instruments of ill omen,
not the instruments of the noble man.
Only when it is unavoidable does he use them,
placing calm and detachment above all.
He does not glorify victory,
and to glorify it
is to delight in the slaughter of men.
Now, one who delights in the slaughter of men
cannot achieve his ambitions in the world.
Therefore, auspicious affairs favor the left,
while inauspicious affairs favor the right.
Thus, the deputy general stands on the left,
and the supreme general stands on the right.
This indicates that it is treated as a funeral rite.
When many people are killed,
it is mourned with grief and tears.
Victory in battle is treated with the rites of a funeral.
The Dao is eternally nameless,
though the Uncarved Block is small,
nothing in the world can subdue it.
If lords and kings could guard it,
all things would naturally pay homage.
Heaven and earth unite, to send down sweet dew,
and without command, the people are naturally equal.
Once institutions arose, there were names.
Since names exist,
one must also know when to stop.
Knowing when to stop avoids danger.
The Dao's presence in the world
is like streams and valleys flowing into rivers and seas.
He who knows others is clever;
He who knows himself is wise.
He who conquers others has strength;
He who conquers himself is mighty.
He who is contented is rich;
He who acts with vigor has will;
He who does not lose his place endures;
He who dies but perishes not enjoys longevity.
The great Tao overflows
and can go left or right.
All things depend on it for life,
yet it does not turn away from them;
its work is accomplished, yet it claims no possession.
It clothes and nourishes all things
yet does not act as their master,
constantly without desire,
it may be named as small;
all things return to it
yet it does not act as their master,
it may be named as great.
Therefore, the sage's ability to achieve greatness
lies in never making himself great,
thus he can accomplish his greatness.
Hold fast to the Great Image,
and all under heaven will come to you;
they come without harm,
and dwell in peace and prosperity.
Music and delicacies
may make passing guests stop for a while.
But the Way, when spoken,
is so bland it has no taste;
look at it—it is not enough to be seen;
listen to it—it is not enough to be heard;
yet use it—it can never be exhausted.
To contract something,
one must surely expand it first;
To weaken something,
one must surely strengthen it first;
To abolish something,
one must surely promote it first;
To take something away,
one must surely give it first;
This is called subtle clarity.
The soft and weak overcomes the hard and strong.
A fish should not leave the deep,
And a state's sharp weapons should not be displayed to others.
The Dao is constantly non-acting,
yet nothing is left undone.
If lords and kings can abide by it,
the myriad things will transform themselves.
When transformation stirs desires,
I will subdue them
with the simplicity of the nameless.
Subduing with the simplicity of the nameless,
they will become desireless.
Being desireless, they will be tranquil,
and the world will settle itself.
The highest virtue is not conscious of itself as virtue,
therefore it truly possesses virtue.
The lower virtue is intent on not losing virtue,
therefore it lacks true virtue.
The highest virtue takes no action and has no ulterior motive;
the lower virtue takes action and has an ulterior motive.
The highest humanity takes action
but without ulterior motive;
the highest righteousness takes action
and has an ulterior motive.
The highest ritual takes action
and when no one responds to it,
one rolls up the sleeves and forces it upon others.
Thus, the Way is lost. After the Way is lost, then comes Virtue;
after Virtue is lost, then comes Benevolence;
after Benevolence is lost, then comes Righteousness;
after Righteousness is lost, then comes Ritual.
Now, Ritual
is the thinning of loyalty and trust,
and the beginning of disorder;
foreknowledge
is the flower of the Way,
and the beginning of folly.
Therefore, the great man
dwells in the thick,
not in the thin;
he dwells in the substance,
not in the show.
Thus, he discards the latter and chooses the former.
Of those that in the past attained the One:
Heaven attained the One and became clear;
Earth attained the One and became tranquil;
Spirits attained the One and became divine;
Valleys attained the One and became full;
The myriad things attained the One and came to life;
Lords and kings attained the One and became the standard of the world.
As for what they attained from it (the One),
It is said that if Heaven were not clear, it would fear splitting;
It is said that if Earth were not tranquil, it would fear upheaval;
It is said that if spirits were not divine, they would fear extinction;
It is said that if valleys were not full, they would fear exhaustion;
It is said that if the myriad things did not live, they would fear perishing;
It is said that if lords and kings were not noble and exalted, they would fear downfall.
Thus nobility takes humility as its root,
eminence takes lowliness as its foundation.
Hence lords and kings
call themselves "the fatherless," "the orphaned," and "the unworthy,"
is this not taking humility as their root?
Is it not so?
Thus seeking excessive praise leads to no praise.
Therefore, one should not wish to be glittering like jade,
but instead be rugged like stone.
Reversion is the movement of the Way,
weakness is the function of the Way.
All things under heaven are born from being,
and being is born from non-being.
When the highest type of scholars hear the Dao,
they diligently practice it;
when the average type of scholars hear the Dao,
they half-believe and half-doubt it;
when the lowest type of scholars hear the Dao,
they laugh heartily at it.
If they did not laugh,
it would not be worthy of being the Dao.
Therefore, the established saying goes:
The bright Way seems dim,
The advancing Way seems retreating,
The smooth Way seems rugged;
The highest virtue seems like a valley,
The purest white seems sullied,
Ample virtue seems insufficient,
Established virtue seems indolent,
Genuine integrity seems changeable,
The great square has no corners,
The great vessel is late in completion,
The great sound is faintly heard,
The great image has no form,
The Way is hidden and nameless.
Yet only the Way is good at lending and completing.
The Dao gives birth to the One,
The One gives birth to the Two,
The Two give birth to the Three,
The Three give birth to all things.
All things carry Yin
And embrace Yang,
Blending Qi to achieve harmony.
What people detest,
are none but solitude, widowhood, and hardship,
yet kings and lords use these as self-references.
Thus, some things may diminish and yet gain,
or gain and yet diminish.
Therefore, the teachings of others,
I also adopt to teach.
So the violent and overbearing
do not meet a natural death,
I shall take this as the fundamental lesson.
The softest thing in the world
gallops through the hardest thing in the world.
That which has no substance enters into that which has no crevice.
Therefore I know the benefit of non-action.
The teaching without words,
the benefit of non-action,
few in the world can attain these.
Fame or body, which is dearer?
Body or goods, which is more valuable?
Gain or loss, which is more harmful?
Therefore, excessive fondness
must lead to great expense,
hoarding too much
must result in heavy loss.
Thus, knowing contentment
avoids disgrace,
knowing when to stop
avoids danger,
and one can endure long.
The greatest perfection seems incomplete,
Yet its use is unimpaired.
The greatest fullness seems empty,
Yet its use is inexhaustible.
The greatest straightness seems bent,
The greatest skill seems clumsy,
The greatest eloquence seems inarticulate.
Movement overcomes cold,
Stillness overcomes heat,
Clarity and stillness can bring order to the world.
When the world follows the Way,
horses are retired to fertilize the fields;
when the world lacks the Way,
warhorses are bred even in the suburbs.
No crime is greater than indulging desires,
no calamity is greater than discontent,
no fault is greater than covetousness.
Thus, the contentment of knowing contentment is eternal contentment.
Without stepping out the door,
one knows the world.
Without peering through the window,
one sees the Way of Heaven.
The farther one travels,
the less one knows.
Thus the sage knows without traveling,
names without seeing,
and accomplishes without acting.
In learning, one increases daily,
in the Way, one decreases daily,
decreasing and decreasing further,
until reaching non-action.
Through non-action,
nothing is left undone.
Governing the world is always through non-interference;
when there is interference,
it is insufficient to govern the world.
The sage has no constant heart,
but takes the heart of the people as his own.
To the good, I am good;
to the not good, I am also good;
thus goodness is attained.
To the faithful, I am faithful;
to the unfaithful, I am also faithful;
thus faithfulness is attained.
When the sage is in the world,
Harmoniously and without bias,
he unifies the heart of the world.
The common people all fix their eyes and ears on him,
yet the sage treats them all as children.
Coming into life and going out to death,
the companions of life are three in ten;
the companions of death are three in ten;
and the people, in their quest for life,
move towards the land of death,
also three in ten.
What is the reason for this?
Because of their excessive striving for life.
I have heard that those who are adept at nurturing life,
when traveling on land do not encounter rhinoceroses or tigers,
and when entering a battlefield do not don armor or bear arms.
The rhinoceros finds no place to thrust its horn,
the tiger no place to sink its claws,
and weapons no place to admit their blades.
Why is this so?
Because they have no realm of death.
The Way gives them life;
Virtue fosters them;
Things give them form;
Circumstances bring them to maturity.
Therefore, all things without exception revere the Way
And honor Virtue.
The reverence for the Way,
The honor for Virtue,
Are not conferred by any decree
But always come spontaneously.
Thus the Way gives them life,
Virtue nurtures them,
Raises them and develops them,
Perfects them and matures them,
Nourishes them and shelters them.
It gives them life yet claims no possession,
It benefits them yet exacts no gratitude,
It leads them yet exercises no control.
This is called profound Virtue.
The world has a beginning,
which is considered the mother of the world.
Having found the mother,
one can thereby know the children.
Having known the children,
return to hold fast to the mother.
And to the end of life, one will be free from danger.
Block the openings,
Close the doors,
And to the end of life there will be no toil.
Open the openings,
Be busy about affairs,
And to the end of life there will be no salvation.
To perceive the subtle is called clarity,
to preserve gentleness is called strength.
Use its light,
and return to its brightness,
leaving no calamity for oneself,
this is called practicing constancy.
If I were to have a sudden moment of clarity,
walking upon the great Way,
I would only fear straying from it.
The great Way is very level and smooth,
yet people are fond of bypaths.
The court is exceedingly corrupt,
The fields are exceedingly barren,
The granaries are exceedingly empty,
Yet they wear embroidered silks,
Carry sharp swords,
Are surfeited with food and drink,
And possess excess wealth and goods.
This is called robbery and ostentation.
Robbery and ostentation—
This is not the Way!
One who is good at building cannot be uprooted,
One who is good at embracing cannot be separated,
So descendants will continue the sacrifices without end.
Cultivate it in the self,
And the virtue becomes genuine;
Cultivate it in the family,
And the virtue becomes abundant;
Cultivate it in the village,
And the virtue becomes enduring;
Cultivate it in the state,
And the virtue becomes plentiful;
Cultivate it in the world,
And the virtue becomes universal.
Therefore observe the individual through the individual.
Observe the family through the family,
observe the community through the community,
observe the state through the state,
observe the world through the world.
How do I know the nature of the world?
Through this.
One who possesses virtue in abundance
is comparable to a newborn infant.
Poisonous insects and venomous snakes do not sting him,
ferocious beasts do not seize him,
birds of prey do not strike him.
His bones are weak, his sinews are soft, yet his grasp is firm.
Without knowing the union of male and female,
yet his organ stirs,
such is the height of vitality.
He may cry all day without becoming hoarse,
such is the height of harmony.
To know harmony is to be in accord with the eternal,
to know the eternal is to be enlightened.
To force the growth of life is ominous,
for the mind to command the vital force is called excessive.
When things reach their prime, they begin to age,
which is contrary to the Way,
and what is contrary to the Way will soon perish.
One who knows does not speak;
one who speaks does not know.
Block the openings,
close the doors,
blunt the sharpness,
untangle the knots,
soften the glare,
settle the dust;
this is called profound unity.
Thus it cannot be approached with intimacy,
nor can it be kept at a distance;
It cannot be benefited,
nor can it be harmed.
It cannot be honored,
nor can it be debased;
Therefore it is honored by all under heaven.
Govern the state with correctness,
employ the army with craft,
and win the world by doing nothing.
How do I know that it is so?
By this.
When the world is full of prohibitions and restrictions,
the people grow poorer.
When the people possess many sharp weapons,
the state and clans become more chaotic.
When people have many clever skills,
strange and exotic things multiply.
When laws and decrees are made more explicit,
thieves and robbers abound.
Therefore the sage says:
I take no action
and the people transform themselves;
I love tranquility
and the people correct themselves;
I engage in no affairs
and the people prosper themselves;
I have no desires
and the people simplify themselves.
When the government is unobtrusive,
the people are simple and honest.
When the government is prying,
the people are needy and crafty.
Misfortune is that upon which blessing depends;
blessing is that in which misfortune is latent.
Who knows its ultimate extent?
Is there no constancy indeed?
The normal reverts to the strange,
The good reverts to the ominous.
People's delusion has indeed lasted long.
Therefore, the sage is square but does not cut,
Sharp-edged but does not pierce;
Straightforward but not unrestrained,
Bright but not dazzling.
In governing people and serving Heaven,
nothing surpasses frugality.
Only through frugality
can one achieve early preparation.
Early preparation
is called the accumulation of virtue.
With the accumulation of virtue,
there is nothing one cannot overcome.
When there is nothing one cannot overcome,
no one knows its limits.
When no one knows its limits,
one can possess a state.
With the mother of the state,
one can endure long.
This is called the way of deepening roots and strengthening the foundation,
for achieving longevity and enduring vision.
Governing a large state is like cooking a small fish.
When the Dào presides over the world,
its ghosts are not supernatural.
It is not that its ghosts are not supernatural,
but that their supernatural power does not harm people.
It is not that their supernatural power does not harm people,
but that the shèngrén also does not harm people.
When neither side harms the other,
virtue merges and returns to them.
A great state is like
the low-lying land where
all streams converge,
the female of the world.
The female always overcomes the male through stillness,
using stillness to take the lower position.
Thus if a great state humbles itself before a small state,
it will win over the small state.
If a small state humbles itself before a great state,
it will be embraced by the great state.
So one humbles itself to win over others,
while the other humbles itself to be won over.
Thus the great state desires only to nurture and protect others,
while the small state desires only to serve and be accepted by others.
When both get what they desire,
it is fitting for the greater to take the lower position.
The Dao is the profound mystery of all things,
The treasure of the good person,
And that by which the not-good are preserved.
Fine words can win respect in the marketplace,
Fine deeds can elevate others.
As for those who are not good,
Why should they be abandoned?
Therefore, when installing the Son of Heaven,
And appointing the Three Dukes,
Though one may present the jade disc preceded by a team of four horses,
It is not as good as sitting and offering this Dao.
Why did the ancients value this Dao?
Did they not say, "Seek and you will obtain,"
"And have your faults forgiven"?
Therefore, it is valued by all under heaven.
Act without acting,
work without working,
taste without tasting.
Regard the small as large, the few as many,
and repay injury with virtue.
Plan for what is difficult while it is easy,
and do what is great while it is small.
The world's difficult matters
must arise from the easy,
and the world's great matters
must arise from the small.
Therefore, the sage never attempts great things,
and thus can achieve greatness.
Those who make promises lightly seldom keep their word;
Those who find everything easy will encounter many difficulties;
Therefore, the sage treats things as difficult,
And thus in the end encounters no difficulties.
What is stable is easy to maintain,
what has not yet shown signs is easy to plan for,
what is brittle is easy to break,
what is minute is easy to scatter.
Act upon it before it comes into being;
govern it before there is disorder.
A tree that fills a man's embrace
grows from a tiny sprout;
a tower nine stories high
rises from a heap of earth;
a journey of a thousand miles
begins beneath one's feet.
Whoever acts will ruin it;
whoever grasps will lose it.
Therefore the sage does not act,
and so does not ruin;
does not grasp,
and so does not lose.
People in handling affairs
often ruin them just as they are nearing completion.
Therefore, if one is as cautious at the end as at the beginning,
then there will be no failed endeavors.
Thus, the sage desires what is not desired,
and does not value rare goods;
learns what is not learned,
and returns to what others have passed by.
In this way, they assist the natural course of all things,
yet dare not act willfully.
In ancient times, those who were skilled in the Way
did not use it to enlighten the people,
but rather to keep them ignorant.
The reason the people are difficult to govern
is because of their abundance of knowledge.
Thus, to govern a state with cunning
is to be a curse to the state;
not to govern a state with cunning
is to be a blessing to the state.
To constantly know these two things
is also a standard to follow.
To constantly know this standard
is called profound virtue.
Profound virtue is deep, far-reaching,
and distant,
opposite to ordinary things.
Only then can it reach great harmony.
The reason why rivers and seas can be kings of all valleys,
is that they excel at staying low,
thus they become the kings of all valleys.
Therefore, when a sage wishes to stand above the people,
they must speak humbly to them;
when they wish to lead the people,
they must place themselves behind them.
Hence, the sage stays above
yet the people do not feel burdened,
stays ahead
yet the people do not feel harmed,
so the world delights in supporting them
and does not grow weary.
Because they do not contend,
no one in the world can contend with them.
All under heaven say that my Way is great,
but seems unlike anything.
It is precisely because it is great that it seems unlike anything.
If it were like anything,
long ago
it would have become small!
I always have three treasures,
which I hold and preserve:
The first is called compassion,
the second is called frugality,
the third is called not daring to be ahead of the world.
Through compassion, one can be courageous;
through frugality, one can be expansive;
not daring to be ahead of the world, one can become a vessel's leader.
Now if one discards compassion, yet is bold,
discards frugality, yet is extravagant,
discards humility, yet seeks precedence,
then one is surely doomed.
For compassion, in battle leads to victory,
in defense ensures firmness.
When Heaven intends to save someone,
it protects them with compassion.
A skilled commander does not show martial prowess,
A skilled warrior does not give in to anger,
A skilled victor does not engage the enemy directly,
A skilled employer places himself below others,
This is called the virtue of non-contention,
This is called employing the strengths of others,
This is called aligning with the ultimate principle of heaven since ancient times.
Those skilled in warfare have a saying:
I dare not play the host but prefer to play the guest,
I dare not advance an inch but would rather retreat a foot.
This is called marching without appearing to move,
rolling up one's sleeves without showing one's arms,
confronting the enemy without seeming to be armed,
grasping weapons without holding them.
No disaster is greater than underestimating the enemy;
underestimating the enemy nearly cost me my treasure.
Thus, when opposing armies meet in battle,
it is the compassionate side that will win.
My words are very easy to understand,
very easy to practice;
yet under heaven none can understand them,
none can practice them.
Words have their ancestor,
deeds have their master.
It is because of ignorance
that I am not understood.
Those who understand me are few,
and thus I am all the more valued.
Therefore the sage wears coarse cloth but holds jade to his breast.
To know when one does not know is best.
To think one knows when one does not know is a disease.
Only by recognizing this disease as a disease
can one be free from it.
The sage is free from this disease
because he recognizes this disease as a disease.
Therefore, he is free from it.
When the people do not fear authority,
then great authority will arrive.
Do not constrain their dwellings,
nor weary their livelihoods.
Only by not wearying them,
will they not grow weary.
Thus, the sage knows himself
but does not display himself,
loves himself but does not exalt himself.
Therefore, he discards that and takes this.
Those who are brave in being daring will be killed,
Those who are brave in not being daring will survive;
These two things, one is beneficial, the other harmful.
What Heaven dislikes,
Who knows the reason?
Therefore, even the sage finds it difficult.
The way of Heaven,
Does not contend, yet excels in winning,
Does not speak, yet excels in responding,
Does not summon, yet comes of its own accord,
Is calm and unhurried, yet excels in planning.
Heaven's net is vast,
Loose, yet nothing slips through.
If the people are always and truly unafraid of death,
how can they be intimidated by the threat of death?
If the people are made to constantly fear death,
and for those who act perversely,
I would capture and kill them,
then who would dare?
If the people are always and necessarily afraid of death, then there should always be an executioner to carry out the killings.
To take the place of the executioner in killing
is like substituting for a master carpenter in chopping wood.
Those who substitute for a master carpenter in chopping wood
rarely avoid injuring their own hands.
The people's hunger,
is because of their superiors' excessive consumption of taxes,
thus they hunger.
The people's difficulty to govern,
is because their superiors have actions
they undertake, thus they are difficult to govern.
The people's disregard for death,
is because of their pursuit of a life that is too rich.
Thus they disregard death.
Only those who do not act for the sake of life,
are wiser than those who value life highly.
When a person is born, they are soft and weak;
when they die, they become stiff and rigid.
All living things, plants and trees, are soft and pliable when alive;
when they die, they become dry and brittle.
Therefore it is said:
The stiff and rigid are companions of death;
the soft and weak are companions of life.
Thus, when an army is strong, it does not prevail;
when a tree is strong, it is cut down.
The strong and great occupy the lower position;
the soft and weak occupy the higher position.
Is not the way of heaven like the stretching of a bow?
The high it presses down,
the low it lifts up;
the excessive it takes from,
the deficient it gives to.
Therefore the way of heaven
diminishes the excessive
and supplements the deficient.
The way of man is not so:
it diminishes the deficient
to offer to the excessive.
Who can take what is excessive
and offer it to the world?
Only one who possesses the Way.
Therefore, the sage acts but does not claim possession,
achieves success but does not dwell on it.
Is it not because they do not wish to display their worth?
Nothing in the world is softer and weaker than water,
yet nothing is better at attacking the hard and strong,
for nothing can take its place.
That the weak overcomes the strong,
and the soft overcomes the hard,
is known by all under heaven,
yet no one can put it into practice.
Therefore the sage says:
To bear the disgrace of the state,
is to be the master of the altars of soil and grain;
to bear the misfortunes of the state,
is to be the king of all under heaven.
True words seem paradoxical.
When great enmity is reconciled,
some enmity is bound to remain;
how can this be considered good?
Therefore the sage holds the left tally
but does not press others for payment.
Thus the virtuous keep their pledges,
while the virtueless exact collections.
The Way of Heaven shows no favoritism -
it constantly accompanies the good person.
A small state with few people,
where even tools that are ten or a hundred times more efficient
are left unused.
Let the people value their lives highly
and not migrate far away.
Though there be boats and carriages,
they find no reason to ride them.
Though there be armor and weapons,
they have no occasion to display them.
Let the people return to the use of knotted cords.
They relish their food,
appreciate their clothing,
feel content in their homes,
and delight in their customs.
Neighboring states are within sight of each other,
the sounds of roosters and dogs are within hearing of each other,
yet the people till old age and death do not interact with each other.
True words are not beautiful,
beautiful words are not true.
The good do not debate,
those who debate are not good.
The wise are not learned,
the learned are not wise.
The sage does not accumulate,
the more he does for others, the more he possesses himself;
the more he gives to others, the more he has himself.
Therefore, the way of heaven benefits without harming;
the way of the sage acts without contending.
